notes.1: Weaker candidates found this question challenging. The most popular incorrect option was D, perhaps because candidates did not recognise the tesla as a unit.
notes.6: Weaker candidates found the analytical demands of this question very challenging, with most of them opting for option B (which involved taking 11.0 s as the time spent accelerating). However, stronger candidates found the question relatively straightforward. �PAGE�2
notes.7: Candidates found this a challenging question, revealing widespread difficulties in understanding of forces acting on a system. Many candidates chose option B, perhaps indicating a misconception that the two forces being compared are related by Newton’s third law.
notes.9: This was another question that candidates found challenging, but in this case the main difficulty that they experienced was in distinguishing between options B and C. Stronger candidates realised that, irrespective of whether the time scale was long enough for terminal speed to be reached (which is unknown in the question), the crucial point was that the gradient of the curve must be equal to the gradient of the initial graph at the point of release.
notes.10: Many candidates found this question challenging with option B preferred by some stronger candidates and option A chosen by many weaker candidates. These options involved finding, respectively, the initial kinetic energy of the rock and omission of the use of conservation of momentum to determine the final speed of the moving piece.
notes.14: A number of weaker candidates incorrectly chose option C.
notes.16: Candidates found this question challenging. Some candidates were distracted by option D, which involved using the diagonal distance rather than the vertical height in the potential energy equation. Other candidates chose option C, which involved making the same mistake but neglecting to take the power needed to drive the escalator against friction into account.
notes.20: A significant minority of weaker candidates were tempted by option A.
notes.23: Weaker candidates found this question difficult, and all four options were chosen.
notes.24: This was challenging for many candidates. Option A was a popular choice. The question revealed some confusion between the conditions required for the formation of stationary waves and the respective conditions required for constructive and destructive interference.
notes.31: Many candidates selected option C, and candidates did not recognise the need for a deeper analysis, based on evaluating the resistance of each lamp that the information in the question (about the resistances remaining unchanged) was designed to prompt.
notes.33: Many weaker candidates did not take into account the polarity of the cells and so chose option D.

notes.general_comments:
Candidates performed particularly well in Questions 4, 5, 14, 15, 20, 22, 38 and 39. Questions 8, 17, 21, 30
and 36 were also answered correctly by most candidates. There were no general trends in topic areas that
candidates found particularly easy or difficult, with a varied performance in questions across each topic area.
However, candidates were more successful in certain types of question than others, with questions involving
pure recall or straightforward calculations particularly well answered. Questions that required deeper
conceptual insight, perhaps including algebraic or graphical analysis, were more challenging. They found
Questions 6, 7, 9, 10, 16, 24, 31 and 37 particularly challenging.
